title: Czechia: Czech Finances and Babiš Conflict-of-Interest Case Cast Shadow Over Prague's… · 11 Sep
keywords: Czech Republic, Agrofert, Andrej Babiš, European Commission, EU subsidies, conflict of interest, Czech budget deficit, public debt, EU fiscal rules, Central Europe, EU funds, Czech politics, Stability and Growth Pact
notes: The European Commission has halted some subsidy payments to companies linked to Prime Minister Andrej Babiš, reigniting a long-running conflict-of-interest dispute that Brussels says remains unresolved. Simultaneously, the Czech government is pushing a 2027 budget with a deficit of 389 billion crowns, drawing sharp criticism from fiscal hawks who warn that public debt is becoming entrenched. Together, the two controversies are testing public trust and Czechia's credibility within the European Union.
